audit.why: Riven owns Levels 1-5 against a melee-range scaling mage with no mobility until 6; 52.31% over 1147 games and a 4/10 difficulty with a 9.5/10 carry threat is the right shape — easy lane, hard game.
Both layers read Riven/Riven/Riven/Riven/Skill/Skill/Kassadin, which matches packet.levelChart exactly and matches the mirror's resolution (First item to Skill, Two+ items to Kassadin).
audit.corrected: No chart edits. Riftwalk at 6 (5/3.5/2s cooldown, 500 range) and AP item scaling justify the two late flips already on the page.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two invented mechanics run through the page. (a) 'Q silence' — Null Sphere has no silence in Riot's text; it deals damage and interrupts channels. (b) 'his passive magic-damage shield' — Void Stone is flat magic damage reduction, not a shield; the shield is on Null Sphere and it absorbs magic damage only.
audit.why: Riven's entire kit is physical, so Null Sphere's shield absorbs none of her damage and there is nothing to 'drain' before committing. Telling the player to spend Levels 1-2 chipping a shield that does not apply to them wastes the one phase they are supposed to be winning, and telling them their W can be silenced makes them hold the stun they should be leading with. The real interaction is the reverse: Ki Burst's stun makes Riftwalk uncastable, so the stun must land before he blinks — he has to blink on the dash-in, not after.
audit.corrected: Silence claims removed from whys[1], whys[3], early, mid and wants.foe[0]. Shield claims corrected in whys[0], spikes[0].text, early and wants.you[0]. edits.before: Level 1 his passive shield absorbs one empowered auto, so open with a Q-auto-Q-auto weave to drain it fast rather than dumping everything into a shielded hit. At Level 2 your W stun is live — the moment he steps forward to Q you for the silence, E into him, pop W before his Q animation lands, and run the Q chain while he is locked down; his passive shield has a recharge delay after absorbing damage so back-to-back autos drain it. Level 3 is your clearest ownership window: full Q-E-W with ignite should take him to a third of HP, and a second trade while he has no Riftwalk escape finishes it — if he burns Flash here the lane is already yours.
edits.after: Level 1 costs him nothing to contest, so trade on your terms: Void Stone only cuts magic damage and Null Sphere's shield only absorbs magic, and every point of your damage is physical. At Level 2 your W stun is live — the moment he steps forward to poke, E into him, pop W before Null Sphere lands, and run the Q chain while he is stunned; Ki Burst is an 11s cooldown at rank 1, so make it count. Level 3 is your clearest ownership window: full Q-E-W with ignite should take him to a third of HP, and a second trade while he has no Riftwalk escape finishes it — if he burns Flash here the lane is already yours.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 you maintain the physical edge but his Q silence starts to matter — if it lands before your W, your stun is silenced and the whole rotation collapses into a losing trade. Step up to trade only when his Q is already on cooldown or his passive shield is visibly down, and wave-manage toward your side so he must overextend to farm rather than Q-poking freely from range. At Level 6 the calculus splits: if you are already ahead, Blade of the Exile plus Wind Slash is a clean kill on Riftwalk's cooldown — E in, full chain, R1 extended-range follow, Wind Slash the execute. If you are even, respect that his Riftwalk goes live simultaneously and that a single blink repositions him past your W range; take the kill only if you can guarantee the stun lands before he can blink.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 you keep the physical edge but Null Sphere chip starts to matter — a 650-range projectile on a 9-to-7s cooldown, and eating it every wave is how an even lane slips away. Step up to trade only when his Q is already spent, and wave-manage toward your side so he must overextend to farm rather than Q-poking freely from range.
